metadata.assessment_title: OWASP Juice Shop Local VAPT Lab Assessment

findings.title: SQL Injection in User Authentication Endpoint
findings.description: The email input field on the login endpoint (/rest/user/login) fails to sanitize SQL metacharacters, allowing arbitrary SQL command execution and authentication bypass.
findings.evidence: Payload: ' OR 1=1-- submitted in email field returned HTTP 200 OK with admin session token.
findings.reproduction_steps:
1. Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:3000/#/login
2. Intercept login POST request in Burp Suite.
3. Replace email with `' OR 1=1--` and password with `password`.
4. Observe successful authentication as Administrator.
findings.impact: Complete compromise of backend database confidentiality and authentication bypass.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized SQL queries (Prepared Statements) or an ORM with proper parameter binding instead of string concatenation.
findings.tester_notes: Verified manually via Burp Suite request repeater.

findings.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Product Search
findings.description: The search parameter on the main page reflects user input directly into the DOM context without proper HTML entity encoding.
findings.evidence: URL parameter `q=<iframe src="javascript:alert(1)">` triggers script execution in user browser context.
findings.reproduction_steps:
1. Access `http://127.0.0.1:3000/#/search?q=<iframe src="javascript:alert(1)">`
2. Observe JavaScript execution pop-up.
findings.impact: Attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's session context, potentially stealing session tokens or hijacking user actions.
findings.remediation: Contextually encode all user-supplied data rendered in the DOM using Angular DOMSanitizer or secure framework encoding.
findings.tester_notes: DOM-based XSS confirmed in search component.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in Shopping Basket API
findings.description: The GET /rest/basket/{BasketID} API endpoint relies solely on the path parameter without enforcing that the requested basket belongs to the authenticated user.
findings.evidence: Authenticated User A (Basket 1) fetched GET /rest/basket/2 and received User B's cart contents and address details.
findings.reproduction_steps:
1. Log in as User A and capture GET /rest/basket/1.
2. Modify path parameter to GET /rest/basket/2.
3. Server returns HTTP 200 OK containing User B's private cart data.
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to other users' sensitive cart and shipping information.
findings.remediation: Implement session-based authorization checks to verify that the requested resource ID belongs to the authenticated user token.
findings.tester_notes: IDOR validated across multiple basket IDs.

findings.title: Absence of Anti-CSRF Protections on State-Changing API Endpoints
findings.description: State-changing operations (such as updating profile details) rely on standard cookies without validating Anti-CSRF tokens or SameSite cookie attributes.
findings.evidence: Automated form submissions do not validate anti-CSRF headers.
findings.reproduction_steps:
1. Host a cross-origin form submitting to http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/Users/
2. Submit form from authenticated browser.
3. Request executes with victim session cookies.
findings.impact: Attacker can trick authenticated users into performing unintended actions.
findings.remediation: Implement Anti-CSRF tokens (Custom Request Headers) or set SameSite=Strict / Lax on session cookies.
findings.tester_notes: Flagged by ZAP passive baseline scan.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers (Content-Security-Policy & HSTS)
findings.description: HTTP response headers lack security baseline hardening such as Content-Security-Policy (CSP), Strict-Transport-Security, and X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.evidence: Response header inspection confirms absence of CSP and HSTS headers.
findings.reproduction_steps:
1. Inspect HTTP response headers via browser network tab or curl.
2. Confirm absence of Content-Security-Policy header.
findings.impact: Increases susceptibility to XSS, clickjacking, and MIME-sniffing attacks.
findings.remediation: Configure web server/middleware to send Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY.

findings.title: Verbose Stack Trace Disclosure on Malformed API Query
findings.description: Sending invalid data types to internal Node.js/Express API routes yields uncaught exception stack traces disclosing internal server file paths.
findings.evidence: Server responded with HTTP 500 containing Sequelize database error and internal file paths (/app/routes/search.js).
findings.reproduction_steps:
1. Send GET request to `/rest/products/search?q='`
2. Observe full JavaScript stack trace in response body.
findings.impact: Exposes technical stack details aiding attacker reconnaissance.
findings.remediation: Disable detailed error messages in production environment (NODE_ENV=production) and implement generic global error handlers.

findings.title: Vulnerable Outdated Components in Node/Angular Stack
findings.description: Application bundles third-party frontend and backend npm packages containing publicly disclosed CVE vulnerabilities.
findings.evidence: Juice Shop version 16.0.0 uses legacy component bundles for educational training.
findings.reproduction_steps:
1. Run npm audit against application source.
2. Review list of vulnerable sub-dependencies.
findings.impact: Vulnerabilities in underlying libraries may allow remote code execution or client-side compromise.
findings.remediation: Regularly audit third-party packages using npm audit and update libraries to secure maintained versions.
findings.tester_notes: Flags known vulnerable dependencies in Juice Shop lab container.
